findings.title: [P1] Keep branch names out of the shell command
findings.body: When `branch` contains shell syntax such as `HEAD; touch /tmp/pwned`, `exec` runs the appended command with the application's privileges rather than passing the value literally to Git. The previous `execFile("git", ["show", branch])` implementation avoided shell interpretation. This also permits unmanaged background processes through metacharacters such as `&`.

findings.title: [P2] Preserve completion and cancellation semantics for refs containing `&`
findings.body:
`&` is valid in Git branch names, but `showBranch("topic&")` now executes `git show topic` as a background shell job. The returned process can report successful exit before Git finishes, and subsequent `kill()` calls cannot cancel that Git process. Previously, `execFile` passed `topic&` literally.

_Recommend validating this comment independently._

findings.title: [P1] Avoid interpolating branch names into a shell command
findings.body:
Any caller-controlled `branch` value can execute arbitrary shell commands. For example, `showBranch("HEAD; rm -rf /target")` runs both `git show HEAD` and the injected command; the previous `execFile` implementation passed the branch as a literal argument without invoking a shell.

_Recommend validating this comment independently._

findings.title: [P1] Restore argument-separated execution to prevent command injection
findings.body:
`exec()` invokes a shell and interpolates `branch` verbatim. Any untrusted branch value such as `HEAD; touch /tmp/pwned #` executes arbitrary commands with the application’s privileges; the previous `execFile()` call treated it only as a Git argument.

_Recommend validating this comment independently._

findings.title: [P1] Avoid spawning unmanaged processes through shell-expanded branch names
findings.body:
On POSIX, a valid branch string such as `missing;yes>leak&` starts a background `yes` process writing indefinitely. The returned `ChildProcess` owns only the shell, so cancellation and `maxBuffer` do not terminate the background process; one request can exhaust disk/I/O, and repeated requests can exhaust the process table.

_Recommend validating this comment independently._
